'''Patricia Hiddleston''' (9 May 1933 – 8 December 2017), also known as '''Pat Hiddleston''', was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[mathematician]] who spent most of her professional career in [[Northern Rhodesia]], central [[Africa]].

== Early life ==
Patricia Wallace was born 9 May 1933 to hotel proprietors Harry and Jessie Wallace of [[Troon]]. She achieved good grades in school and went on to study mathematics and [[natural philosophy]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]]. She graduated in 1956 with a double first and was awarded the Napier medal for mathematics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fortitervivamus.co.uk/the-patricia-hiddleston-scholarship-edinburgh-university-school-of-mathematics/|title=The Patricia Hiddleston Scholarship – Edinburgh University School of Mathematics|last=Redmond|first=Cecile|date=18 March 2019|website=St Margaret's School, Edinburgh FP Association|language=en-GB|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-30}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/opinion/15815856.obituary-pat-hiddleston-scots-mathematician-and-teacher-who-helped-shape-education-in-africa/|title=Obituary - Pat Hiddleston, Scots mathematician and teacher who helped shape education in Africa|last=|first=|date=9 January 2018|website=The Herald (Scotland)|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-30}}</ref>

== Career ==
In July 1956 she graduated and, the same month, married George Hiddleston and became Pat Hiddleston.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://commonwealthwomensvoices.wordpress.com/2009/11/24/pat-hiddlestone/|title=Pat Hiddleston|last=|first=|date=24 November 2009|website=Voices: commonwealth women and education|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-30}}</ref> She and her husband applied to the [[Colonial Office]] for a posting abroad and were allocated to [[Northern Rhodesia]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/obituaries/obituary-pat-hiddleston-educationalist-mathematician-consultant-and-adviser-1-4649748|title=Obituary: Pat Hiddleston, educationalist, mathematician, consultant and adviser|last=|first=|date=1 January 2018|website=The Scotsman|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-30}}</ref>

Hiddleston worked at [[Munali Secondary School]], then a teacher training college near [[Lusaka]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/alumni/services/profiles/graduation/1950s/pathiddleston|title=Patricia Hiddleston|website=The University of Edinburgh|date=24 June 2015 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-30}}</ref> She studied for a doctorate at the [[University of South Africa]] and was subsequently made the first member of the mathematics department of the [[University of Zambia]], where she lectured from 1965–1970.<ref name=":1" />

After 14 years, Hiddleston and her family returned to Scotland so that the four children could have higher education there.<ref name=":2" /> Hiddleston was the Headmistress of [[St Margaret's School, Edinburgh]].

In 1984, Hiddleston relocated to South Africa to become the Principal of [[Durban Girls' College]], where she oversaw the school's move to admit all races.<ref name=":1" />

Hiddleston then went to teach mathematics education<ref name=":1" /> at the [[University of Malawi]] in 1988. She continued this work until her husband's death in 1996, after which she moved into a consulting career involving advising governments on encouraging women into STEM studies and teacher training and development.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

Hiddleston also co-wrote and edited a number of textbooks.<ref name=":1" />

== Later life, death, and commemoration ==
Hiddleston volunteered at the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and was honoured by the University of Edinburgh Institute of Mathematics for life services to maths education in 2015.<ref name=":3" />

Hiddleston continued to work until age 82, when she became ill whilst on a trip to Bangladesh and was diagnosed with ovarian cancer.<ref name=":1" />

In 2018, the University of Edinburgh began offering a Patricia Hiddleston Summer Scholarship.<ref name=":0" />
